questions.q: Where are #temp tables and @table variables physically stored?
options: Both live in tempdb
Temp tables live in tempdb; table variables live only in memory and never touch disk
Both live in the user database
Table variables live in tempdb; temp tables live only in memory
questions.explain: Both are backed by tempdb — the real difference is in statistics, scope, and transaction behavior, not physical location.

questions.q: What is the biggest practical difference between a #temp table and a @table variable for large result sets?
options: SQL Server maintains real statistics on a temp table, letting the optimizer build a much smarter plan than for a table variable
Table variables can never hold more than one row
Temp tables cannot be indexed
Table variables always run faster no matter the size
questions.explain: Statistics let the optimizer estimate row counts accurately; without them (as with table variables, historically), the optimizer can badly misjudge resource needs.

questions.q: What happens to a CTE's underlying query if you reference the same CTE three times in one statement?
options: SQL Server may re-run the underlying query multiple times, since nothing is stored
It's automatically cached after the first reference, always
It throws a syntax error
It's converted into a permanent table
questions.explain: A CTE isn't materialized by default — each reference can re-evaluate the underlying query, though SQL Server sometimes spools it on its own.

questions.q: How does a #temp table behave inside a transaction that gets rolled back?
options: It's rolled back along with the transaction
It survives the rollback intact
It's automatically converted to a table variable
It causes the rollback to fail
questions.explain: Unlike a table variable, a temp table's changes are rolled back with an enclosing transaction.

questions.q: Per the lesson's decision rule, when should you reach for a table variable?
options: A handful of rows, inside a procedure, wanting to avoid recompiles
Millions of rows that need their own custom index
Recursive hierarchy traversal
Whenever a CTE would also work, since they're identical
questions.explain: Table variables shine for small row counts where avoiding plan recompilation matters more than having real statistics.
